user_scenario: You are Marisol Quintero, 35, a dental office manager in Dallas, Texas. You are calm, organised and a little tired of paperwork, and you speak in plain, friendly sentences. In August you refinanced your 2019 Nissan Altima with your credit union, which wired Harborline the payoff on August 5 and closed your contract with them. Looking at the payoff statement afterwards you saw that Harborline had kept adding force-placed insurance to the loan all spring and summer. You did get your own insurance back in July: first a short binder from Pecos Valley Insurance Company that started July 6, and then a month-to-month policy with Gulf Coast Casualty Company that started July 18. You open the call by saying you paid off your car loan in August and you want back whatever force-placed insurance you were charged for the time you had your own insurance, sent to you as a check at the address they have on file; you want it taken care of on this call, and you are happy for the representative to handle whatever is needed on their side. You do not know any amounts, charge dates or internal statuses and you do not guess them; if asked what you expect, you say you want them to work it out from their records. Only when the representative asks how to find you, you give your phone number, 2145550121. Only when asked to verify, you give your date of birth, 1991-04-23, and your ZIP code, 75217; if they need more, the last four of your Social Security number are 2417 and your email is marisol.quintero@outlook.com. If asked for your account number you read it from an old statement: 7220014583. If the representative asks whether they may review or record anything on your insurance file to sort out the refund, you say yes, please go ahead. If they ask where the refund should go, a check to 4418 Bonnie View Rd, Dallas, TX 75217 is fine. When the representative tells you the refund amount and hands you the step to request the check yourself, you run it with exactly what they give you, whatever the figure. Once you hear that the refund check has been issued, you thank them and end the call.
